title: Microsoft Teams: organisers can delete meeting recording, transcript and AI notes from the recap
summary: Hold: the briefing treats retention protection as unconfirmed even though Microsoft's retention rules cover deleted files in OneDrive and SharePoint. It also assigns an unsupported add-on requirement to the delete button and omits important exceptions for recording storage and recap without transcripts.

claims.claim: Deleting the generated content is one click from the recap.

claims.claim: Users can manually delete recordings before expiry unless a Purview retention policy prevents it.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A recording manually deleted during its retention period is held in the Preservation Hold library.
claims.quote: If a user manually deletes a recording that's still in the retention period, the recording is held in the Preservation Hold library. However, the recording shows as deleted to the end user.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview protection for content deleted through the recap is unconfirmed because Learn documents retention only for manually deleted recordings.
claims.quote: All files stored in SharePoint (and SharePoint Embedded) or OneDrive sites can be retained by applying a retention policy or retention label.
claims.fix: Replace the broad caveat with 'Purview retention covers files in OneDrive, SharePoint and SharePoint Embedded; deleting an item subject to retention preserves its original content for compliance. The exact set of artifacts removed by the recap button remains to be confirmed.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-policies-sharepoint. Remove the assertion that expiry, retention and eDiscovery all assume content leaves on a chosen schedule. Keep pilot testing as advice, not as evidence that file retention is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Recordings of meetings and events are saved to the organiser's OneDrive.
claims.quote: For Channel meetings, the recording is stored in the SharePoint Teams site documentation library in a folder named Recordings.
claims.fix: In both places replace the unconditional storage statement with 'For non-channel meetings, recordings normally save to the organiser's OneDrive; channel meeting recordings save to the channel's SharePoint site. If the organiser has no OneDrive, storage falls back to a co-organiser or the recording initiator.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/tmr-meeting-recording-change.

claims.claim: Attendees in the organiser's organisation were given read access to the recording.
claims.quote: All other members of the meeting from the same organization as the organizer have read access, but no sharing and download permissions.
claims.fix: Narrow the sentence to 'For ordinary non-channel meetings, other internal attendees normally have read access to the recording; some participants in large meetings may not receive access automatically, and channel meetings inherit channel permissions.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Deleting content removes it from attendees' ordinary view even if a compliance copy is retained.
claims.quote: If a user manually deletes a recording that's still in the retention period, the recording is held in the Preservation Hold library. However, the recording shows as deleted to the end user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes organiser-driven deletion, not new data access or automatic or agent-driven deletion.
claims.quote: Meeting organizers can now easily delete meeting generated content including recording, transcript, AI summary, and notes through the new delete button in recap page. Shared files in the meeting won't be deleted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Deleting or expiring a transcript or recording does not automatically delete meeting memory.
claims.quote: Meeting memory won't automatically be deleted if the transcript or recording is deleted or expired.

claims.claim: Users can change the expiration of recordings they control, so expiration is not legal protection on its own.
claims.quote: End users can modify the expiration date of any recordings they control, so you shouldn't rely on meeting expiration settings for legal protection.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: The delete capability is an add-on because the recap it sits in requires Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "delete" "recap" "license" "charge"; Teams delete recap content licensing basic recap Teams Premium meeting recording delete. Read recap licensing and Teams Premium comparison: they license intelligent experiences, not this delete operation or all recap access.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the notes with 'Teams use requires a Teams licence. No requirement specific to the recap delete button is published. Intelligent recap separately requires Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot; recap without saved transcripts requires Microsoft Copilot.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Replace 'The recap it sits in needs a Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot licence' with 'Intelligent recap requires Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot.' Remove the premise in Open questions that all recap already requires that add-on.

claims.claim: Intelligent recap needs transcription turned on.
claims.quote: With this feature, an AI summary is generated even when recording and transcription aren't enabled.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn says intelligent recap needs transcription turned on' with 'The full intelligent recap experience requires transcription; intelligent recap without saving transcripts can generate an AI summary even when recording and transcription are not enabled.' Keep both existing recap sources.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription reaches the transcription control.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true enables transcription under that meeting policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Recording & transcription > Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire reaches automatic expiry.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire setting in the Teams admin center under Meetings > Meeting policies > Recording & transcription.
claims.fix: Use 'Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire'. The policy selection is an omitted target-picking step, not a wrong route.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days> sets the recording and transcript expiration period.
claims.quote: To set the expiration time using PowerShell, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days>

claims.claim: Changing the recording expiration setting affects only newly created recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: Any changes to this setting only affect newly created recordings and transcripts. You can't change the expiration time on existing meeting recordings and transcripts.

claims.claim: The stated policy route through Copilot and other AI reaches the default Intelligent Recap .docx expiration control for non-transcribed meetings.
claims.quote: Under Copilot and other AI, next to Set a default expiration time for Intelligent Recap .docx files for non-transcribed meetings, enter the number of days that documents are retained.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays 180 sets the AI summary document expiration to 180 days.
claims.quote: The following example sets the default expiration time to 180 days. Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays 180

claims.claim: The document expiration control accepts 1 to 9999 days, or -1 for no expiration.
claims.quote: You can specify a value from 1 to 9999 days, or -1 for no expiration.

claims.claim: A Teams admin can delete a meeting memory file using Remove-AIGeneratedKnowledge -ThreadId <String> -CallId <String>.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Teams admin can also delete a meeting memory file through PowerShell: ... Run the following command (ThreadId is required; CallId is optional) ... Remove-AIGeneratedKnowledge -ThreadId <String> -CallId <String>

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; controls notes; Governance controls
claims.claim: A request to disable the button cannot be met by any policy change today, and the listed policies cannot stop its use.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy recap deletion prevent delete recap content. Read recap without transcripts, meeting memory and policy syntax. AllowIntelligentRecap can disable intelligent recap for all meetings; no source establishes the effect on the new delete button.
claims.fix: Replace the absolute policy claim with 'No policy setting specifically for the recap delete button is documented as of November 2026.' In the notes say 'These rows document transcription and expiration controls, not a button-specific switch.' Do not infer that no broader policy change can affect its availability.

claims.claim: The checklist calls transcription the first controls row and the expiry controls the second and third rows.

claims.fix: Change '(first controls row)' to '(second controls row)' and '(second and third controls rows)' to '(third and fourth controls rows)'.

claims.claim: Purview file retention takes precedence over Teams recording expiration.
claims.quote: File retention takes precedence over file deletion. A Teams meeting recording expiration policy can't delete a Teams meeting recording with a Purview retention policy until after the retention period is completed.
